significance: A Jain tirtha on the ancient mound of Ahichchhatra in Bareilly district, held to be the place where Parshvanatha, the twenty-third Tirthankara, attained kevala jnana. Both Digambara and Svetambara establishments stand here; the Digambara temple was rebuilt in 1975 and further shrines added in 2002 and 2007, on a site whose antiquities run back to the Indo-Scythian, Kushan and Gupta periods.
story: While Parshvanatha meditated, a demon is said to have flooded him to the neck, whereupon the serpent king Dharanendra spread a thousand-hooded canopy above him and the goddess Padmavati coiled about his body to hold him clear of the water.
